title: Versatile Datapath Soft Error Detection on the Cheap for HPC Applications
problem: Modern microprocessors are increasingly susceptible to soft errors that corrupt datapath units due to technology downscaling and lower voltage levels. Existing error detection solutions either provide limited protection or impose massive performance and power overheads, preventing practical deployment.
motivation: Efficient soft error detection in HPC applications is essential to maintain system reliability while avoiding the prohibitive performance penalties of existing approaches.
method: CONDA analyzes the source code before compilation to understand what arithmetic operations it performs, then adds checking code during compilation that catches errors in those operations when the program runs. These runtime checks are made efficient because the analysis was done beforehand. The added checks don't change when decisions happen in the program or what data gets read and written.
key_novelty: By analyzing programs before they run and using those insights to make runtime error checks efficient, this approach detects errors in processor arithmetic circuits while using significantly less computing overhead than other methods.
contributions: CONDA: a novel compile-time code transformation and static analysis framework for datapath soft error detection
Low-overhead runtime error detection mechanism maintaining program semantics and structure
41.84% performance improvement over state-of-the-art with equivalent error detection capability
Comprehensive evaluation on 38 benchmarks and HPC simulation demonstrating practical viability with 57.79% runtime overhead
primary_theme: efficient datapath soft error detection for HPC
